message.reasoning:
We need to produce JUnit 4 test cases covering all methods of Whitelist. The output must start with ###Test START## and end with ###Test END##. Provide a Java file with imports, test class, test methods.

We need to test:

- static factory methods: none(), simpleText(), basic(), basicWithImages(), relaxed()
- addTags, removeTags
- addAttributes, removeAttributes (including :all)
- addEnforcedAttribute, removeEnforcedAttribute
- preserveRelativeLinks
- addProtocols, removeProtocols
- isSafeTag (protected, but can test via reflection or subclass? Could make a subclass exposing it.)
- isSafeAttribute (protected) - test via subclass exposing public wrapper.
- testValidProtocol indirectly via isSafeAttribute with protocols.
- isValidAnchor, getEnforcedAttributes.

We can create a test class WhitelistTest with inner subclass exposing protected methods.

We'll need to create Elements and Attributes. Use jsoup library classes: Element, Attribute. For simplicity, we can create an Element via new Element(Tag.valueOf(...)). But Tag class is internal; we can use new Element(Tag.valueOf("a")). Actually Tag class is jsoup.nodes.Tag; need import org.jsoup.nodes.Tag; but may not be present? We can use Element(String tagName) constructor? In Jsoup, Element has a constructor Element(Tag tag, String baseUri). Simpler: new Element(org.jsoup.parser.Tag.valueOf("a"), ""); Actually Tag is in org.jsoup.parser.Tag. Use org.jsoup.parser.Tag.

We'll create Element el = new Element(Tag.valueOf("a"), "http://example.com"); Then add attribute.

Test addAttributes: after adding, isSafeAttribute should return true for allowed attribute.

Test removeAttributes: after removal, false.

Test :all attribute removal.

Test enforced attribute: after adding, isSafeAttribute should accept attribute only if matches enforced value.

Test remove enforced attribute.

Test addProtocols: ensure only allowed protocols accepted. For example, addProtocols("a","href","http","https"); test with attribute value "http://example.com" passes; "ftp://example.com" fails.

Test removeProtocols: after removal, attribute without protocol restrictions.

Test preserveRelativeLinks: when false, attribute value set to absolute; when true, preserve relative.

Test isSafeTag: after addTags.

We'll need reflection to call protected methods, but we can subclass WhitelistTestHelper extends Whitelist with public wrappers.

E.g., class TestableWhitelist extends Whitelist { public boolean isSafeTagPublic(String tag){ return super.isSafeTag(tag);} public boolean isSafeAttributePublic(String tag, Element el, Attribute attr){ return super.isSafeAttribute(tag, el, attr);} }

Now write test methods.

Edge cases: adding duplicate tags, attributes.

Testing removeTags also removes related maps.

Test removeProtocols with invalid removal should throw IllegalArgumentException (Validate.isTrue). Use expected exception.

We'll need to import junit.framework.Assert? Use org.junit.Assert.

Now produce final output.
